Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 84, verse 2:

In the sense of "it listened to its Lord, and it was right for it to do so," as ʿAdiyy ibn Zayd said:

Indeed my concern lies in hearing (samaʿ) and ear (udhun),

in the sense of "in listening (samaʿ) and hearkening (istimaʿ)."

(A benefit)

It is written in a clean vessel: ﴿When the sky is split open, and it hearkens to its Lord and it is right that it should; and when the earth is stretched out, and casts out what is within it and empties itself﴾

The pregnant woman drinks from it, and it is sprinkled over her belly.

If the pronoun refers back to the deed, then it means seeing it recorded in the Book, written down and inscribed.

And if it refers back to the Lord, glorified and exalted be He, then it means meeting Him, which He promised.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 84, verses 7–8:

It is established in the Sahih (the authentic collection) from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever has his account scrutinized will be punished."

So ʿĀʾishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, does not Allah say: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to a easy account﴾?"

He said: "Yes, but that is merely the presentation (al-ʿardh); whoever has his account scrutinized will be punished."

The reconciliation of the two texts was difficult for her until he explained to her that there is no contradiction between them, and that the easy reckoning is the presentation (al-ʿardh) in which Allah makes clear to every doer his deeds, as He, the Exalted, says: ﴿On that Day you will be exposed; not hidden among you is any secret﴾ [al-Haqqah: 18].

Then, when a person thinks that he will not be saved, Allah, the Exalted, saves him by His pardon, His forgiveness and His mercy; but if the reckoning scrutinizes him, He will certainly punish him.

(Section)

Among these is His oath by ﴿the twilight, and the night and what it gathers, and the moon when it becomes full﴾.

So He swore by three things related to the night. The first is al-shafaq (twilight), which linguistically is the redness after the sun sets until the time of the late evening prayer (salat al-'isha'), and so it is in the sharia as well.

Al-Farra', al-Layth, al-Zajjaj and others said: al-shafaq is the redness in the sky. The root meaning of the letters is the thinness of a thing, and from it comes "shay' shafaq," a thing with no firmness due to its thinness; and from it comes al-shafaqa (compassion), which is tenderness, and ashfaqa 'alayhi, meaning he felt tenderness toward him.

The people of language say al-shafaq is the remnant of the sun's light and its redness. For this reason, the correct view is that the shafaq whose disappearance marks the entry of the time of the late evening prayer is the redness.

Since the redness is the remnant of the sun's light, its persistence was made the limit of the time of maghrib. When the redness departs, the sun has moved further from the horizon, and so the time of 'isha' begins.

As for the whiteness, its time extends with the length of its duration, and it occurs while the sun is further from the horizon. For this reason it is authentically reported from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: al-shafaq is the redness. The Arabs say "a garment dyed as if it were shafaq" when it is red, as al-Farra' related.

Likewise al-Kalbi said: al-shafaq is the redness that appears in the west. Similarly Muqatil said: it is what occurs after the sun sets on the horizon before the darkness.

'Ikrima said: it is the remnant of the day, and this may mean that this redness is the remnant of the sun's light, which is the sign of the day.

Mujahid said: it is the whole day.

This is very weak, and it seems that when he saw it paired with the night and what it gathers, he thought it was the day, but this is not necessary.

The second: His oath by the night and what it gathers, i.e., what it contains, encompasses and collects. The night and what it contains and encompasses is another sign, the moon is a sign, and its becoming full is another sign.

The twilight includes the retreat of the day, which is a sign, and the advance of the night, which is another sign. For when one retreats, the other follows, the two alternating for the benefit of creation. So the retreat of the day is a sign, the advance of the night is a sign, and one succeeding the other is a sign. The twilight, which includes both matters, is a sign; the night is a sign; what it gathers is a sign; the crescent is a sign; its growth each night is a sign; its becoming full, which is its being full of light, is a sign; then its beginning to wane is a sign.

These and similar things are signs indicating His lordship, necessitating knowledge of His attributes of perfection. For this reason, at the advance of the night and the retreat of the day, the remembrance of the Lord, exalted is He, was legislated in the maghrib prayer.

And in a hadith:

"O Allah, this is the advance of Your night, the retreat of Your day, and the voices of Your callers, so forgive me, and the presence at Your prayers, forgive me."

Just as the remembrance of Allah was legislated in the dawn prayer at the retreat of the night and the advance of the day. For this reason He, glorified is He, swears by these two times, as in His saying ﴿and the night when it retreats, and the morning when it brightens﴾, which corresponds to His oath by the twilight.

Its counterpart is His oath by ﴿the night when it departs, and the morning when it breathes﴾.

Since the Lord, blessed and exalted, causes to arise, at each of the two extremes of the advance and retreat of night and day, what He causes and disperses among His creation as He wills: He spreads the satanic spirits at the advance of the night, and spreads the human spirits at the advance of the day, and this dispersal has its effect on the world. For this reason He, glorified is He, legislated these two great prayers at these two times, along with the remembrance of Him at these two alternating signs, and at the ending of one and the connection of the other to it, together with the opposition and difference between them, and the transition of living beings at that time from one state to another and from one ruling to another. This is a daily observable beginning and return for creation, every day and night: animals and plants are in a beginning and a return, and the age of the world is in a beginning and a return. ﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed that is easy for Allah.﴾

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 84, verse 19–21:

"Ayy: state after state" (i.e., one condition after another).

The first of its layers ("aṭbāq") is that he is a sperm-drop (nuṭfah), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqah), then a lump of flesh (muḍghah), then a fetus (janīn), then a newborn (mawlūd), then a suckling infant (raḍīʿ), then one weaned (faṭīm), then healthy or sick, rich or poor, sound or afflicted — up to all the varied states that befall a human being until he dies, then is resurrected, then is made to stand before God, then goes on to Paradise or the Fire.

So the meaning is: "You will surely traverse state after state, station after station, and affair after affair."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: "You will surely [experience] one stage in the Hereafter after the first; you will surely become rich after poverty and poor after wealth."

ʿAṭāʾ said: "Hardship after hardship."

The word ṭabaq and ṭabaqah means "state." Hence it is said: "So-and-so was in various stages (ṭabaqāt shattā)."

ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: "Indeed I was in three stages (ṭabaqāt thalāth)," meaning states.

Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "Ṭabaq is a state with all its variations."

And he said in (al-Tibyān):

As for His saying ﴿لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ﴾ ("You will surely traverse layer after layer"), the apparent reading is that it is the answer to the oath. It is also permissible that it is the answer to an omitted oath, and "latarkabunna" and what follows is a new (independent) statement.

It is also read "latarkabanna" with a dammah on the bāʾ for the plural, and with a fatḥah. Whoever reads it with a fatḥah, the address according to him is to the human being, i.e., "You will surely traverse, O human." It was also said that it refers to the Prophet specifically. It was also said that the tāʾ is not for address but for the third person, i.e., "The sky will surely traverse layer after layer." Whoever reads it with a dammah, the address is to the group only. Whoever makes the pronoun refer to the sky says the meaning is: "The sky will surely traverse state after state of its states, which Allah the Exalted described: splitting, cleaving, folding up, being like molten metal at one time and like red leather at another, its orbits, its opening, and other of its states."

This is the saying of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu), and the mention of twilight (al-shafaq) and the moon indicates the sky. On this view, it is an oath concerning the Return and the transformation of the world.

Whoever says the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) has three meanings: "You will surely traverse sky after sky until you reach where Allah ascends you."

This is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās in a narration from Mujāhid, and the saying of Masrūq and al-Shaʿbī. They said: "The sky is a layer (ṭabaq)." Hence the seven heavens are called "the layers" (al-ṭibāq).

The second meaning: "You will surely ascend degree after degree, station after station, rank after rank, until you reach the place of nearness and closeness to Allah."

The third meaning: "You will surely traverse state after state of the varied states in which Allah transfers His Messenger: the emigration, the struggle, his victory over his enemy, the enemy's triumph over him at times, his wealth and poverty, and other of his states through which he was transferred until he reached what Allah brought him to."

Whoever says the address is to the human being or to humankind as a whole, the meaning is one: the human's transition from state to state, from the time he is a sperm-drop until his abode in Paradise or the Fire. How many layers and states lie between these two for the human being!

All the statements of the exegetes revolve around this.

Ibn ʿAbbās (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhumā) said: "Matters will surely change state after state." It was also said: "You will surely traverse, O human, state after state: from sperm-drop to clot, to lump of flesh, to being alive, to his coming out into this world; then his traversing a layer of discernment between what benefits him and what harms him; then his traversing after that another layer, which is the layer of puberty; then his traversing the layer of full strength; then the layer of old age; then the layer of decrepitude; then his traversing the layer of what follows death in the barzakh. His traversing during these states many layers, in which he continuously moves from state to state until the abode of settlement. That is the last of his layers known to the servants. After that, Allah, glorified is He, does what He wills."

Abū ʿUbaydah preferred the reading with a dammah and said: "The meaning is more fitting to people than to the Prophet, for before the verse He mentioned those given their book in their right hand and those given their book in their left, then after it He mentioned His saying: ﴿فَما لَهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ('Why then do they not believe?')."

So He mentioned their becoming layer after layer. Al-Wāḥidī said: "This is the saying of most exegetes. They said: 'You will surely traverse state after state, station after station, affair after affair.'"

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: "You will surely [experience] one stage in the Hereafter after the first; you will surely become rich after poverty and poor after wealth."

ʿAṭāʾ said: "Hardship after hardship." Abū ʿUbaydah said: "You will surely follow the way of those before you in denial and in disagreement regarding the messengers."

When you reflect on this sworn-by and sworn-about, you find it among the greatest signs indicating Lordship, and Allah's transforming of the world and directing it as He wills, moving it from state to state.

It is impossible that this should happen by itself without a directing agent, and it is impossible that its agent be incapable, not living, not willing, not wise, not knowing; both are equally impossible.

So what is sworn by and sworn about is among the greatest proofs of His lordship, His oneness, His attributes of perfection, His truthfulness, the truthfulness of His messengers, and of the Return. For this reason He follows it with His saying ﴿فَما لَهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, rebuking those who do not believe after these signs have appeared, which necessitate what they signify most completely. He also rebukes them for not humbling themselves and prostrating before the Qur'an, which contains all this in the most eloquent, clear, comprehensive and concise expression. Thus the meaning is the most noble meaning, and the expression is the most noble expression: ultimate truth with ultimate clarity and eloquence.

He also rebukes them for not humbling themselves and prostrating before the Qur'an, which contains all this in the most eloquent, clear, comprehensive and concise expression. Thus the meaning is the most noble meaning, and the expression is the most noble expression: ultimate truth with ultimate clarity and eloquence.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 84, verse 19–21:

"Ayy: state after state" (i.e., one condition after another).

The first of its layers ("aṭbāq") is that he is a sperm-drop (nuṭfah), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqah), then a lump of flesh (muḍghah), then a fetus (janīn), then a newborn (mawlūd), then a suckling infant (raḍīʿ), then one weaned (faṭīm), then healthy or sick, rich or poor, sound or afflicted — up to all the varied states that befall a human being until he dies, then is resurrected, then is made to stand before God, then goes on to Paradise or the Fire.

So the meaning is: "You will surely traverse state after state, station after station, and affair after affair."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: "You will surely [experience] one stage in the Hereafter after the first; you will surely become rich after poverty and poor after wealth."

ʿAṭāʾ said: "Hardship after hardship."

The word ṭabaq and ṭabaqah means "state." Hence it is said: "So-and-so was in various stages (ṭabaqāt shattā)."

ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: "Indeed I was in three stages (ṭabaqāt thalāth)," meaning states.

Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "Ṭabaq is a state with all its variations."

And he said in (al-Tibyān):

As for His saying ﴿لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ﴾ ("You will surely traverse layer after layer"), the apparent reading is that it is the answer to the oath. It is also permissible that it is the answer to an omitted oath, and "latarkabunna" and what follows is a new (independent) statement.

It is also read "latarkabanna" with a dammah on the bāʾ for the plural, and with a fatḥah. Whoever reads it with a fatḥah, the address according to him is to the human being, i.e., "You will surely traverse, O human." It was also said that it refers to the Prophet specifically. It was also said that the tāʾ is not for address but for the third person, i.e., "The sky will surely traverse layer after layer." Whoever reads it with a dammah, the address is to the group only. Whoever makes the pronoun refer to the sky says the meaning is: "The sky will surely traverse state after state of its states, which Allah the Exalted described: splitting, cleaving, folding up, being like molten metal at one time and like red leather at another, its orbits, its opening, and other of its states."

This is the saying of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu), and the mention of twilight (al-shafaq) and the moon indicates the sky. On this view, it is an oath concerning the Return and the transformation of the world.

Whoever says the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) has three meanings: "You will surely traverse sky after sky until you reach where Allah ascends you."

This is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās in a narration from Mujāhid, and the saying of Masrūq and al-Shaʿbī. They said: "The sky is a layer (ṭabaq)." Hence the seven heavens are called "the layers" (al-ṭibāq).

The second meaning: "You will surely ascend degree after degree, station after station, rank after rank, until you reach the place of nearness and closeness to Allah."

The third meaning: "You will surely traverse state after state of the varied states in which Allah transfers His Messenger: the emigration, the struggle, his victory over his enemy, the enemy's triumph over him at times, his wealth and poverty, and other of his states through which he was transferred until he reached what Allah brought him to."

Whoever says the address is to the human being or to humankind as a whole, the meaning is one: the human's transition from state to state, from the time he is a sperm-drop until his abode in Paradise or the Fire. How many layers and states lie between these two for the human being!

All the statements of the exegetes revolve around this.

Ibn ʿAbbās (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhumā) said: "Matters will surely change state after state." It was also said: "You will surely traverse, O human, state after state: from sperm-drop to clot, to lump of flesh, to being alive, to his coming out into this world; then his traversing a layer of discernment between what benefits him and what harms him; then his traversing after that another layer, which is the layer of puberty; then his traversing the layer of full strength; then the layer of old age; then the layer of decrepitude; then his traversing the layer of what follows death in the barzakh. His traversing during these states many layers, in which he continuously moves from state to state until the abode of settlement. That is the last of his layers known to the servants. After that, Allah, glorified is He, does what He wills."

Abū ʿUbaydah preferred the reading with a dammah and said: "The meaning is more fitting to people than to the Prophet, for before the verse He mentioned those given their book in their right hand and those given their book in their left, then after it He mentioned His saying: ﴿فَما لَهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ('Why then do they not believe?')."

So He mentioned their becoming layer after layer. Al-Wāḥidī said: "This is the saying of most exegetes. They said: 'You will surely traverse state after state, station after station, affair after affair.'"

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: "You will surely [experience] one stage in the Hereafter after the first; you will surely become rich after poverty and poor after wealth."

ʿAṭāʾ said: "Hardship after hardship." Abū ʿUbaydah said: "You will surely follow the way of those before you in denial and in disagreement regarding the messengers."

When you reflect on this sworn-by and sworn-about, you find it among the greatest signs indicating Lordship, and Allah's transforming of the world and directing it as He wills, moving it from state to state.

It is impossible that this should happen by itself without a directing agent, and it is impossible that its agent be incapable, not living, not willing, not wise, not knowing; both are equally impossible.

So what is sworn by and sworn about is among the greatest proofs of His lordship, His oneness, His attributes of perfection, His truthfulness, the truthfulness of His messengers, and of the Return. For this reason He follows it with His saying ﴿فَما لَهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, rebuking those who do not believe after these signs have appeared, which necessitate what they signify most completely. He also rebukes them for not humbling themselves and prostrating before the Qur'an, which contains all this in the most eloquent, clear, comprehensive and concise expression. Thus the meaning is the most noble meaning, and the expression is the most noble expression: ultimate truth with ultimate clarity and eloquence.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 84, verses 22–25:

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny.﴾ They do not affirm the truth, out of obstinate rejection and stubbornness. ﴿And Allah knows best what they conceal.﴾ That is, what they harbour in their breasts and hide, what they secretly do of deeds, and what they gather; He will recompense them for it with His knowledge and justice. ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward never to be cut off.﴾

(Benefit)

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment, except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward never to be cut off.﴾

Here, it is very far-fetched to assume that the exception (al-mustathna) is included in what precedes it. Rather, this is a report of what awaits each of the two groups: when He gave the disbelievers the tidings of punishment, He gave the believers the tidings of a reward never to be cut off.

This is from the type of al-mathani (the paired style, mathani meaning "the twofold" or "repeated pairs"), in which a thing is mentioned together with its opposite, like the Exalted's words: ﴿Indeed, the righteous are in bliss, and indeed, the wicked are in the Blazing Fire.﴾

Thus there is no hidden element (muqaddar) from which this exception is excluded. And Allah knows best.
